name: multiple_choice: An EPA analyst works with a data frame containing…

request.questionText: An EPA analyst works with a data frame containing information on virtually every model of vehicle offered for sale to U.S. consumers during 2020, including the following variables: make -- one of 41 car manufacturers. The baseline category of this variable is Acura. city -- city gas mileage in miles per gallon highway -- highway gas mileage in miles per gallon displacement -- engine size in liters emissions -- emissions of carbon dioxide (CO2), measured in grams of CO2 per mile driven powertrain -- vehicle engine type: Diesel, EV, FFV, Gasoline, Hybrid, or Plug-in Hybrid category -- type of vehicle: Car, Small Car, SUV/Van, Truck, TwoSeater, Wagon They fit a regression model to predict highway gas mileage in terms of engine displacement and vehicle type category: lm(highway ~ displacement + category, data=cars) %>% get_regression_table(digits=1) %>% select(-std_error, -statistic, -p_value) producing the following results: Based on this regression table, which of the following statements is accurate? Choose the best answer.

choices.label: A
choices.text: For vehicles in the SUV/Van category, we expect a decrease of 7.5 highway miles-per-gallon for a one-liter increase in engine displacement.

choices.label: B
choices.text: We are 95% confident that vehicles in the Wagon category get between 0.2 and 3.3 fewer highway miles per gallon for a one-liter increase in engine displacement.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Vehicles in the Car category get between 38-40 highway miles-per-gallon.

choices.label: D
choices.text: When comparing vehicles with the same engine displacement, we expect a decrease in highway miles-per-gallon for each vehicle category relative to the baseline Car category.
